stimulus.source_note: Photograph: Betty Friedan, 1960 (Fred Palumbo, New York World-Telegram and Sun photograph, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons); the photograph was viewed before writing. Account drawn from the grounding books and verified against NOW's own history: NOW was founded in June 1966; Friedan's The Feminine Mystique was published in 1963; Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 banned sex discrimination in employment.
stimulus.text:
The photograph shows Betty Friedan in 1960, three years before her book The Feminine Mystique was published.

In the book, Friedan wrote that many educated, middle-class wives felt confined and unfulfilled in the role of full-time homemaker, though they had been told that role should make them happy. In June 1966, Friedan helped found the National Organization for Women (NOW). NOW pressed the government to enforce the ban on sex discrimination in jobs in the Civil Rights Act of 1964 and worked for equal pay and equal opportunity for women.

stem: Why was the National Organization for Women founded in 1966?

options.text: To win women the right to vote in federal elections
options.misconception: Background: Women won the right to vote with the Nineteenth Amendment in 1920, more than forty years before NOW was founded.

options.text: To protest the Supreme Court's decision in Roe v. Wade
options.misconception: Background: Roe v. Wade was decided in 1973, seven years after NOW was founded.
The Nineteenth Amendment gave women the vote; NOW did not seek to repeal it.

options.text: To enforce the job-discrimination ban Congress had already passed

rationales.A: Background: Women won the right to vote with the Nineteenth Amendment in 1920, long before NOW was founded.
rationales.B: Background: Roe v. Wade was decided in 1973, seven years after NOW was founded in 1966.
rationales.C: Background: The Nineteenth Amendment gave women the vote, and NOW did not seek to repeal it.
rationales.D: The passage says NOW pressed the government to enforce the ban on sex discrimination in jobs in the Civil Rights Act of 1964.
rationales.general:
1. Congress had already banned sex discrimination in jobs in the Civil Rights Act of 1964.
2. But a law on the books does not enforce itself.
3. The passage says NOW pressed the government to enforce that ban and worked for equal pay and equal opportunity.
4. Background: NOW also pressed the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission to act on complaints from women.
Remember: Winning a law and making the law work are two different fights, and NOW was founded for the second one.
